card.name: Hunguhungu
card.era: Post-1797 Garifuna diaspora in Central America; rooted in St. Vincent culture (1635 ethnogenesis)
card.tagline: Women's swaying circular dance in triple time, secular echo of the sacred dügü.
card.profile: Hunguhungu (also 'hüngühüngü' or 'fedu') is a circular swaying dance performed chiefly by Garifuna women, distinctive for being in 3/4 (triple) meter rather than the usual duple-time Garifuna rhythms. Dancers form circles or lines, swaying their hips side to side while singing call-and-response, accompanied by the primero (treble) and segunda (bass) drums plus gourd shakers (sísira). It is described as the secular version of the adugurahani, the sacred drum/dance form of the dügü ancestor ceremony (English Wikipedia; Smithsonian Folkways).
card.insight: Hunguhungu is a vehicle for women's communal expression and social commentary, with lyrics addressing loss, current events and community concerns; it falls under the UNESCO 2001/2008 inscription of Garifuna language, dance and music (English Wikipedia; UNESCO).
